items.title: Joe Muranyi interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 11, 2007
items.q: He said, “Ray Sinatra’s big band was rehearsing and I wanted to see what it was and you came up with me, and who’s playing baritone sax but Kenny Davern. ctx.x: Yeah. We were there and Pops was on that, Pops Foster. And backstage he comes up to me and grabs me and there I am playing with Louis Armstrong, his old buddy. It was wonderful. I had some wonderful moments that way. So anyway I get into the milieu playing with this guy, that guy, you know, and I’m taking lessons. I took lessons with Lennie Tristano for a long time. And you know I didn’t dislike modern jazz, I just couldn’t do it. And so I used to buy all the records and try to keep up to date and all that kind…

what it was and you came up with me, and who’s playing baritone sax but Kenny Davern. And Kenny was interested in what we were doing and he came down and played his clarinet. And he said that’s where you first met him. It’s a long time ago. But I’ve got to tell you the truth, Kenny Davern was, very early on, a wonderful clarinet player. It was just, he was God given natural you know. I think that Bob Wilber is a great reed man too but I think Kenny is more creative.
